extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for the Branco Weiss Fellowship (ETH Zurich)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for postdoctoral researchers worldwide applying to the Branco Weiss Fellowship, including eligibility, project expectations, reviewer/invitation letter requirements, and the selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to engage in dialogue across disciplines and societal issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship provides a platform for exceptionally qualified researchers from all disciplines demonstrating a willingness to engage in a dialogue on relevant social, cultural, political, or economic issues across the frontiers of their particular discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is international and transdisciplinary in nature; applicants should show readiness to interact beyond their narrow disciplinary boundaries and address broader societal questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: career stage and faculty status
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have officially completed their PhD by the application deadline, and they should not have received their PhD more than five years ago. Faculty members (assistant professors or lecturers) or former faculty members are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your PhD completion date falls within the five-year window and that you are not currently or formerly holding faculty positions (assistant professor, lecturer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline openness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Branco Weiss Fellowship is open to researchers at postdoctoral level in all disciplines (including natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and humanities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from any academic discipline may apply; the program explicitly welcomes cross-disciplinary approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project must exploit new avenues of research (novelty & transdisciplinarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a project that exploits new avenues of research, often transdisciplinary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should push into new directions, bridge disciplines, and take intellectual risks that benefit from the fellowship's unique freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project should depart significantly from mainstream research
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects which depart significantly from mainstream research and will profit from the unique freedom offered by the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how the project would not fit conventional funding or employment structures and how the fellowship's flexibility is essential for its success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of outstanding achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide evidence of outstanding achievement in their particular scientific field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document prior accomplishments (publications, awards, impact) that demonstrate exceptional performance relative to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection evaluates scientific ability, personal qualities, and motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual number [of fellowships] depends on the performance of the applicants during the interviews, taking into account not only scientific abilities of the candidates, but also their personal qualities and motivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to be assessed holistically in interviews—scientific excellence alone is insufficient; convey personal drive, fit, and motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestion independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant should not stand in any scientific relationship to the suggested persons, which means that they should not have published together, have worked together, or plan to work together. It is fine, if they have been in contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When naming referees, avoid collaborators and people with current or planned scientific relationships to you; prior informal contact is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation letter: signature and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The invitation letter should be signed by your potential host professor and describe why you and your project are deemed to be excellent and why the host institution offers the most suitable environment to carry out the research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain a letter from the main host professor that explicitly endorses both the candidate and the project's fit with the host environment, stressing resources, supervision, and institutional suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation letter requirement for multiple hosts
rubrics_metrics.description: If planning to work at more than one host institution: No, we do only request an invitation letter from the main host resp. from the institution where you will start the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single invitation letter from the primary host even if the project spans multiple institutions; clarify secondary collaborations within the proposal if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial support structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial support is given to fellows in the form of a project grant. This is administered by the host institution via a three-way contractual agreement between the fellow, their chosen institution(s), and ETH Zurich.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to work with your host institution on contractual and administrative arrangements; funding is project-based and routed through the host.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection procedure and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: All incoming applications are screened. Letters of recommendation and external reviews will be requested once the applicant has been short-listed. A final selection of applicants will be invited for interviews to present their project to the Directorate and selected faculty members of ETH Zurich in Zurich, Switzerland. The decision is typically communicated to candidates within two weeks after the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect an initial screening, possible external reviews after shortlisting, an in-person interview in Zurich for finalists, and a rapid decision post-interview; plan references and travel accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of fellowships awarded per year
rubrics_metrics.description: The program aims to award up to ten fellowships each year. The actual number depends on the performance of the applicants during the interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a fixed number of awards; competitive performance in interviews influences final award numbers.
